model.title: CIPZIP Act of 2025
model.meta: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee · Sen. James Lankford (R-OK)

summary.text: The bill would require the Postal Service to set up a public process letting state, local, and Tribal governments request changes to ZIP code boundaries or new ZIP codes, with criteria covering feasibility, cost, and future address needs. Denied requesters would receive a written reason, a designated contact, and one appeal, and would be barred from resubmitting a substantially similar request for five years. A seven-year pilot program would let governments pay to cover the Postal Service's net costs so that cost alone does not block a requested change. The Postal Regulatory Commission would report on the pilot each year, and the bill would leave the Postal Service's other authority over mail and facilities unchanged.
